extracted.intended_audience: European Union institutions, Member State governments, national IP authorities, and WIPO/International Bureau officials
extracted.subtask_description: Legal/administrative rules approving the European Union's accession to the Geneva Act of the Lisbon Agreement on Appellations of Origin and Geographical Indications, and specifying representation, notifications, declarations, voting and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of accession on behalf of the Union
rubrics_metrics.description: The accession of the European Union to the Geneva Act of the Lisbon Agreement on Appellations of Origin and Geographical Indications is hereby approved on behalf of the Union (Article 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text of the Geneva Act is attached to the Decision. This Approval is the formal act by which the Union expresses consent to be bound by the Geneva Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation to deposit instrument of accession
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the Council shall designate the person empowered to deposit, on behalf of the Union, the instrument of accession provided for in point (ii) of Article 28(2) of the Geneva Act, to express the consent of the Union to be bound and to make the declaration and notification attached to the instrument of accession (Article 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The designated person will deposit the instrument of accession and attach the declarations/notifications required by this Decision (see Article 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Member State ratification/accession alongside the Union (authorization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Member States which wish to do so are authorised to ratify or to accede, as appropriate, alongside the Union the Geneva Act in the interest of the Union and in full respect of its exclusive competence (Article 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such ratification/accession by Member States is permitted but must respect the Union's exclusive competence; the Decision contemplates parallel instruments by Member States only where consistent with Union competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission represents Union (and ratifying Member States) in Special Union
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Special Union, the Union and any Member States which ratify or accede to the Geneva Act pursuant to Article 3 shall be represented by the Commission in accordance with Article 17(1) TEU; the Union shall be responsible for ensuring the exercise of the rights and fulfillment of the obligations of the Union and of those Member States (Article 4(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation in the Special Union is centralized: the Commission acts on behalf of the Union and the indicated Member States; the Union retains responsibility for rights/obligations under the Geneva Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission designated as Competent Authority for administration and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall be designated as the Competent Authority referred to in Article 3 of the Geneva Act, responsible for the administration of the Geneva Act in the territory of the Union and for communications with the International Bureau of WIPO under the Geneva Act and the Common Regulations (Article 4(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This designates the Commission as the Union's operational contact point for administering the Geneva Act and interacting with WIPO and applying the Common Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission to make all necessary notifications under the Geneva Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall make all the necessary notifications under the Geneva Act on behalf of the Union and those Member States (Article 4(1) / Article 4(2) context).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications to WIPO (e.g., deposits, declarations, notifications required by the Geneva Act and Common Regulations) are to be performed by the Commission on behalf of the Union and the Member States that ratify/accede pursuant to Article 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union voting in Assembly; Member States refrain from voting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Union shall vote in the Assembly of the Special Union and the Member States which have ratified or acceded to the Geneva Act shall not exercise their right to vote (Article 4(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the Union's single voting role in the Assembly; Member States that have ratified/acceded must abstain from exercising separate voting rights in the Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration extending specified time-limits per Article 29(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with Article 29(4) of the Geneva Act, a declaration attached to the instrument of accession shall specify an extension by one year of the time limit referred to in Article 15(1) of the Geneva Act, and the periods referred to in Article 17 of the Geneva Act, in accordance with procedures in the Common Regulations (Article 5(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Decision requires this specific one-year extension declaration be attached to the Union's instrument of accession, aligning with the Common Regulations' procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification specifying application particulars for protection in Union territory
rubrics_metrics.description: Per point (a) of Rule 5(3) of the Common Regulations, a notification to the Director‑General of WIPO attached to the instrument of accession shall specify that, for protection in the territory of the Union, an application must, in addition to mandatory contents set out in Rule 5(2), indicate particulars concerning: for an appellation of origin — the quality or characteristics of the good and its connection with the geographical environment of the production area; for a geographical indication — the quality, reputation or other characteristic of the good and its connection with the geographical area of origin (Article 5(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This imposes additional Union-specific particulars that applications must include to obtain protection within the Union, and references the Common Regulations and Rule 5 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of Union's exclusive competence over Geneva Act areas
rubrics_metrics.description: The Union has exclusive competence for the areas covered by the Geneva Act; Member States should not have national protection systems to protect agricultural designations of origin and geographical indications of third country members of the Special Union (recital and paragraph 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recitals note existing Union-wide systems for wines, spirits, aromatised wines and other agricultural products, and explain that accession enables the Union to exercise its exclusive competence in these areas; national systems for third-country protections are discouraged where Union competence applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification/accession by Member States must respect Union competence and Union responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratification or accession by the Member States should fully respect the exclusive competence of the Union, and the Union shall remain responsible for ensuring the exercise of the rights and fulfilment of the obligations of the Union and the Member States under the Geneva Act (recital and Article 4(1) context).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Member States' parallel actions (ratify/access) are permissible only insofar as they do not infringe Union exclusive competence; the Union retains ultimate responsibility for compliance and exercising rights under the Geneva Act.
